Probe lands on a comet

By A. Writer

The probe touched down on the comet's nucleus at 14:02 UTC on Tuesday after a seven-hour descent, the mission team said. It is the first soft landing on a comet that is still active.

Engineers had worried that the surface would be too hard for the anchoring harpoons. Telemetry shows both harpoons fired and held, and the lander is now drawing power from its solar panels.

The lander carries ten instruments. Over the next sixty hours it will drill into the surface, analyse the gases released by the comet, and send images of the landing site back to Earth through the orbiter.

"This is the moment we waited ten years for," the flight director said. The team will decide on Thursday whether to move the lander to a sunnier spot.

Comets are thought to preserve material from the early solar system. Measuring the ratio of heavy to normal water in the ice could show whether comets brought water to Earth.
